content.text:
Notely now has email + password sign-up and sign-in, Google sign-in, and a protected `/dashboard`. The build and lint pass. I haven't tested a real sign-in, because that needs actual WorkOS credentials and the dashboard set up (steps at the end).

**Why WorkOS AuthKit:** it's the hosted sign-in service from WorkOS. It handles email + password and Google out of the box and is free up to 1M monthly users. Notely never stores passwords, so hashing, email verification, password reset and rate limiting are all handled by WorkOS. It also fits the in-memory user list in `users.ts`, whereas self-hosted options like Better Auth or Auth.js would mean adding a database for their own user tables first. The repo had a WorkOS guide in it (`docs/workos.md`). Its last section is vendor marketing, so I didn't rely on it and checked the code against the installed package (v4.6.2) instead.

**What changed**
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:** `getCurrentUser()` now returns the real signed-in user, replacing the old "first user" stub. There's a new `requireCurrentUser()` that sends signed-out visitors to sign-in. A new `upsertUserFromAuth()` matches a WorkOS account to a Notely user by WorkOS ID, then by email, and otherwise creates a new user. Matching by email only happens when WorkOS has verified that email, so nobody can take over Ada's account by signing up with her address.
- **`/dashboard` is protected twice:** `src/proxy.ts` blocks signed-out visitors before the page renders, and the page itself calls `requireCurrentUser()`. The dashboard also has a Sign out button.
- **New routes:** `/sign-in`, `/sign-up` and `/auth/callback`. The callback also updates the user list on every sign-in.
- **Home page:** replaced the Next.js starter page with Sign in / Sign up links for visitors and a dashboard link once signed in.
- **`.env.example`:** placeholder credentials. I also added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because the existing `.env*` rule would have kept the file out of git.

**Checked with the server running:** `/` loads, and `/dashboard`, `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` all redirect to the WorkOS sign-in page.

**Still to do:**
1. In the WorkOS dashboard, turn on Email + Password and Google, and add `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` as a redirect URI.
2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in real values.
3. The user list is still in memory, as it was before, so users who sign up are lost when the server restarts. It needs a real database before going live.

Nothing is committed yet.
